conclusions.scope: Single model and host. Notifications plus any blocking fallback; no claim of universal superiority.

selection.dismissRule: Only consider a strategy with 4/4 verified tasks and zero active notifications after every turn; choose lower median cost. Otherwise retain single.

utilityControl.expected: A random producer fact is available through injection and unavailable in the zero-job-call ablation.
utilityControl.limitation: An ablation of this harness, not proof that other event architectures cannot provide the same capability.

negativeControl.expected: A random producer fact is available through injection and unavailable in the zero-job-call ablation.
negativeControl.limitation: An ablation of this harness, not proof that other event architectures cannot provide the same capability.

limitations: Costs are tariff-based estimates, not billing invoices.
One model and host; exploratory samples do not establish general superiority.
Local workers are controlled real subprocesses with timed waits, not production CI workloads; fixture edits, file tests and GitHub workflows are real executions.

GitHub has two valid pairs per outcome: exploratory only. Runner scheduling and cancellation delays are uncontrolled; whole-turn differences cannot be attributed solely to notifications. Remote job timestamps and local receipt times are preserved separately.
Zero MCP tools/call does not exclude the MCP connection and initialization.
No proactive wake-up and no HTTP ingress while Pi is stopped.
Notifications do not interrupt a running inference or tool: exposure waits for the next context boundary.
Reaction is measured at final structured submission; it is an upper bound for earlier understanding.
Blocking fallback and all notification lifecycle calls count in the metrics.
Polling prompts specify minimum waits; actual agent-chosen waits remain in the raw trace.
Functional negative control intentionally lacks the external result and is not an efficiency baseline.

limits: First triplet tests an in-memory prototype; second tests the applied persistent metadata implementation.
Notification facts are intentionally repeated in common tool results for equal information in all variants. This isolates caching and proves no productivity advantage.
One initial cache miss before notifications arrive exists in fixed-pair2 and current-pair2; exact provider cause unobserved. Full-episode costs retain it.
Archive snapshots increase context size; no zero-overhead or long-session claim. No model/tool/output overrides.
Six short episodes, no statistical significance or exact billing inference. Old pilot outcomes remain untouched.

coordinatorReview.scope: Completed cache-fix subagent delivery; no additional inference
coordinatorReview.finding: Request-local snapshots disappeared from later model inputs even though they were placed at the tail. Retaining immutable historical snapshots at their original conversation-prefix anchors restored cache growth in the measured native Codex runs.
limits: Warm subset does not replace complete-run totals; initial native cache misses remain included.
Archived snapshots remain in model context and add tokens; this is one active queue plus historical observations.
Long sessions and high notification volumes were not measured.
The controlled cache fixtures do not measure notification productivity benefits.
Default journal behavior is scoped to native openai-codex-responses; other providers remain unverified.
Existing single-section benchmark validators need adaptation before a full journal benchmark campaign.
This review does not retroactively establish the cause of every earlier pilot cache miss.

metricDefinitions.modelHttp: Every actual outbound model HTTP attempt, including provider retries; distinct from logical responses and tool calls.
metricDefinitions.toolCalls: Tool execution starts; calls to MCP, native tools, dismiss/history and waits remain distinguishable.
metricDefinitions.tokenTotal: Cumulative tokens over requests, including cached input and reread context; not unique conversation size.
metricDefinitions.nativeCacheFraction: cacheRead / (uncachedInput + cacheRead); historical cacheWrite also contributes to total input denominator.
metricDefinitions.historicalTurnTime: wallMs: prompt to verified end; totalWallMs additionally includes measured startup.
metricDefinitions.pilotTurnTime: Observed actor turn; group duration is the longest actor turn, not sum of overlapping durations.
metricDefinitions.cacheDuration: Short fixture episode duration; not a task-efficiency estimate.
metricDefinitions.reaction: Observable code action or structured submission, not private model understanding.
metricDefinitions.cost: Frozen tariff API-equivalent estimate, not subscription billing; reasoning tokens are within output.
metricDefinitions.unknown: Null means unavailable, not zero. Initial behavior stage and Codex coordinator/subagent usage are outside the tracked totals.
